subject: VM: evidence request — priority routing, remediation SLAs and proof-of-fix
messages:
From: ComplianceTeam@finsecure.com
To: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
Cc: auditor@kc-audits.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: evidence of vulnerability management cadence and remediation SLA mapping

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this. As part of the SOC 2 & SIG review for FinLedger we need a concise set of artifacts showing Redwood's vulnerability management program for the past 90 days. Specifically we need: 
- scan cadence (authenticated/internal and external),
- escalation & routing policy for critical/urgent CVEs (who owns, how incidents are routed),
- stated SLAs for remediation by severity, and
- a short proof-of-fix bundle for 3 representative CVEs affecting customer-facing services.

Can you provide these by EOD PT on Sep 2? If you have an attestation PDF that maps these items to control IDs that would be ideal.

Appreciate it — we can extend the timeline if you need more time.

— Compliance Team (FinSecure)

From: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
To: ComplianceTeam@finsecure.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: evidence of vulnerability management cadence and remediation SLA mapping

Hi —

We can deliver the requested artifacts. Quick summary up front and attachments below: 

1) Scan cadence
- Internal authenticated scans: weekly (every Sunday, full authenticated scan across all infra + container images).
- External perimeter scans: monthly (external host/edge scan).
- Continuous agent-based findings: real-time via our AM/agent fleet (alerts flow to SRE).

2) Routing & ownership
- Critical (CVSS >=9 / exploitable): PagerDuty -> SRE on-call -> immediate remediation playbook; product owner owns rollback/feature gating.
- High (7.0-8.9): assigned to component owner; remediation target 7 calendar days.
- Medium/Low: triage and scheduled by product teams; target 30 days / next release.
- We maintain a vulnerability roster (component -> primary owner) in the vulnerability tracker.

3) SLAs (committed)
- Critical: mitigate within 48 hours (mitigation includes fix, compensating control, or approved exception);
- High: mitigate within 7 days;
- Medium: mitigate within 30 days;
- Exceptions documented and approved by security.

4) Proof-of-fix examples (attachments)
- weekly-internal-scan-2027-08-29.pdf (authenticated scan results, redacted IPs),
- cve-incident-log-2027-07-15.csv (three representative CVE rows with ticket IDs, patch IDs, timestamps),
- SOC2 attestation: soc2-vm-attestation-20270901.pdf (signed by me as Head of Security Compliance).

Notes: We use an internal pipeline that correlates scanner findings to Jira tickets (example: RDW-2345) and pushes fixes to our CI/CD release flow; the scan -> ticket -> patch -> deploy timestamps are included in cve-incident-log. External auditor access can be granted to a read-only bucket if you need the full raw reports.

Uploading attachments now. Let me know if you need the raw Nessus output or additional artifact mapping to SIG/CAIQ control IDs.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Security Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: weekly-internal-scan-2027-08-29.pdf (PDF, 1.4MB), cve-incident-log-2027-07-15.csv (CSV, 8KB), soc2-vm-attestation-20270901.pdf (PDF, 12KB)

From: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
To: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: evidence of vulnerability management cadence and remediation SLA mapping

Thanks Tessa — this looks good. A couple of internal asks before we send the final bundle to FinSecure: 

- Can we include a small CSV that maps the three example CVEs to patch IDs and deploy artifacts (e.g., docker image sha / release tag)? That is the most efficient proof-of-fix for auditors.
- Confirm the escalation path diagram — I'll add a one-page flowchart to the attestation PDF showing PagerDuty -> SRE -> Product owner -> Legal for exceptions.
- For Critical SLA (48h), please include a short note on measurement (how we calculate start time). We start clock at detection (scanner timestamp) or external report time, whichever is earlier.

I'll prepare the additional flowchart and the CSV template; Marcus can validate the deploy IDs against release history.

-Neha
Director, Security Operations

From: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
To: ComplianceTeam@finsecure.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, auditor@kc-audits.com
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 17:37:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: evidence of vulnerability management cadence and remediation SLA mapping — bundle delivered

Hi —

Per our timeline, attached is the evidence package for FinLedger's SOC 2 review: 
- vm-evidence-bundle-20270901.zip (contains full scan JSON exports with redacted IPs and the patch-to-ticket mapping),
- soc2-vm-attestation-20270901.pdf (signed statement mapping controls to artifacts),
- fix-list-20270901.csv (three representative CVEs with ticket, patch ID, release tag, deploy timestamp).

Short clarifying points included in the attestation:
- "Start time" for SLA measurement is the earliest of (scanner detection timestamp, external report timestamp).
- Critical handling: PagerDuty alerts escalate immediately to SRE on-call; we require either an applied fix, a documented compensating control, or an approved exception within 48 hours.
- The routing table is maintained in our vulnerability tracker and includes on-call rotation and primary owners per component.

If auditors need a temporary read-only link to raw scan artifacts, reply and we will provision access for the requested window.

Thanks — please confirm receipt.

Best regards,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Security Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: vm-evidence-bundle-20270901.zip (ZIP, 4.8MB), soc2-vm-attestation-20270901.pdf (PDF, 13KB), fix-list-20270901.csv (CSV, 3KB)
